canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: I confirmed epic-reviewer-1's zero-smooth regression, the related test-coverage gap, and the shared architecture-shim observation. The disagreement with epic-reviewer-2 is explained by scope: `npm run verify-all` passes on current code, but the passing suite never proves that an explicit `smooth: 0` rebuild stays empty. Direct execution of the current builder/materializer path and the real `runSmartCompact()` command shows that an empty smooth selection is still repopulated from the full-fidelity boundary, so the epic cannot close as-is. I did not find evidence to upgrade the remaining `context-*` shims to a blocker because the tech design explicitly allows temporary compatibility scaffolding and the shims point to real implementations.
crossStoryFindings: Story 4 still leaks legacy smooth-band defaulting into Story 5: an explicit `100/0/0/0` rebuild is not authoritative because `ThreadViewMaterializer` repopulates the smooth band after the builder selects none, and `runSmartCompact()` uses that same rebuild path.

The current Story 4/5 suite stays green because the zero-smooth cases only assert full-fidelity selection, threshold behavior, and skipped write/reload outcomes; they never assert that the smooth band or generated PI output remains empty.
architectureFindings: `ThreadViewMaterializer` still gives an empty smooth band one implicit meaning: legacy defaulting from the full-fidelity boundary. Feature 3 deterministic rebuilds need a second meaning for an explicitly empty operator-selected smooth band, and that distinction is not encoded in the current API.

Feature 3's surface migration remains partial. The tech design says the repo should stop deepening `context-steward` / `context-workbench` names and treat compatibility shims as temporary scaffolding, but several production-facing `thread`, `thread-view`, `workbench`, and command files still re-export from or import those older modules.
epicCoverageAssessment: `npm run verify-all` passed locally on current code: 285 unit tests, 10 integration tests, and 34 E2E tests all passed.

Coverage is still incomplete around explicit zero-allocation band mixes. The existing `100/0/0/0` cases do not assert smooth-band emptiness in the rebuilt view or in a successful generated PI file, so the confirmed regression escapes the gate.
I did not find evidence against the placeholder/non-semantic lower-band contract; those paths remain explicit and test-backed.
productionPathFindings: I did not find a fake write or fake reload path. The real smart-compact flow prepares async-thread state, rebuilds a draft view, writes and archives PI-target output, and reloads through the harness adapter, and that path passed the epic gate.

I directly reproduced the zero-smooth regression on the production command surface: `runSmartCompact()` with `requestedBandPercentages: { fullFidelity: 100, smooth: 0, detailed: 0, brief: 0 }` and a permissive lower bound wrote a PI JSONL file containing three `smooth_turn` entries, confirming the Story 4 defect reaches Story 5 output.

blockingFindings.title: Zero-percent smooth allocations still emit smooth-band content
blockingFindings.evidence: `selectTurnIds()` returns an empty selection when the smooth budget is `<= 0` (`src/thread-view/services/thread-view-builder.ts:208-217`), and `buildDraftThreadView()` persists that selection into `smoothBand` (`src/thread-view/services/thread-view-builder.ts:589-645`). `ThreadViewMaterializer.deriveDefaultSmoothBand()` then repopulates any empty smooth band from turns older than the full-fidelity boundary (`src/thread-view/services/thread-view-materializer.ts:180-217`). I reproduced this on current code with the existing deterministic rebuild fixture: `buildDraftThreadView({ requestedLowerBound: 40, requestedBandPercentages: { fullFidelity: 100, smooth: 0, detailed: 0, brief: 0 }, mode: "strict" })` returned a ready draft whose `smoothBand.selectedIds` were `["turn-oldest","turn-middle-older","turn-middle-newer"]` and whose emitted messages included three smooth entries. Because `runSmartCompact()` delegates directly to `buildDraftThreadView()` (`src/commands/smart-compact.ts:131-135`), the same band mix also wrote a generated PI file containing three `smooth_turn` entries. This conflicts with the tech design's explicit per-run rebuild contract (`docs/spec-build/epics/03-deterministic-band-and-projection-mechanics/tech-design-thread-view.md:103-137`).

nonBlockingFindings.title: Zero-smooth regression is not covered by the current Story 4/5 assertions
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: The builder's `100/0/0/0` case in `tests/thread-view/thread-view-builder.test.ts:74-124` asserts the full-fidelity turn selection and threshold degradation only; it never asserts that `smoothBand.selectedIds` is empty or that no smooth-band emitted messages exist. The command-level `100/0/0/0` cases in `tests/commands/smart-compact.test.ts:565-630` assert degraded threshold behavior and skipped write/reload, but they never inspect a successful generated PI file for zero-smooth purity. That is why `npm run verify-all` still passes while the confirmed regression remains live.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Feature 3 surface migration still ships with compatibility shims on the production path
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: The tech design says Feature 3 should stop deepening the older `context-steward` / `context-workbench` names and treat compatibility shims as temporary migration scaffolding (`docs/spec-build/epics/03-deterministic-band-and-projection-mechanics/tech-design.md:240-243`). Current production-facing code still routes through those surfaces in multiple places, including `src/thread/store/file-thread-store.ts:1`, `src/thread/domain/records.ts:1`, `src/thread/store/thread-store.ts:1`, `src/thread-view/store/file-thread-view-store.ts:1`, `src/thread-view/domain/thread-view-records.ts:1`, `src/workbench/services/workbench-query-service.ts:1`, `src/thread-view/domain/pi-thread-view-file.ts:1`, and `src/commands/smart-compact.ts:1-4`. These are real implementations rather than fake adapters, so I do not see a closeout blocker, but the boundary cleanup is still incomplete.

unresolvedItems: Correct the builder/materializer contract so deterministic rebuilds can preserve an explicit empty smooth selection instead of invoking legacy smooth-band defaulting.
Add a regression that exercises a successful `100/0/0/0` smart-compact run and proves both the rebuilt draft view and the generated PI file omit smooth-band content.

crossStoryFindings: Feature 2's legacy 'empty smooth band means derive everything older than full-fidelity' behavior still leaks into Feature 3 deterministic rebuilds, so explicit per-run band mixes are not authoritative when the requested smooth allocation is 0%.

The same drift propagates from Story 4 into Story 5 because `runSmartCompact()` delegates to `buildDraftThreadView()`, so a command intended to produce full-fidelity-only output can still write extra smooth-band messages into the generated PI session file.

The current Story 4/5 test suite passes because it validates the full-fidelity slice for the `100/0/0/0` case but never asserts that the smooth band stays empty, leaving the cross-story regression undetected.
architectureFindings: `ThreadViewMaterializer` currently has one implicit semantic for an empty smooth band (`deriveDefaultSmoothBand`) but Feature 3 needs two distinct semantics: legacy workbench defaulting and explicit deterministic rebuild selections. The API does not encode that distinction, which is why the builder's empty selection is overwritten during materialization.

The surface rename described in the tech design is only partially realized in production code: several `thread`, `thread-view`, `workbench`, and command modules still route through `context-steward` / `context-workbench` re-exports or direct imports, so the architecture boundary migration remains incomplete.
epicCoverageAssessment: `npm run verify-all` passed, and the deterministic loop has strong coverage for smoothing, chunk lifecycle, placeholder generation, rebuild/materialization, PI-target write/archive, and reload sequencing.

Epic coverage is incomplete around explicit zero-allocation band mixes. The passing suite does not currently prove AC-4/AC-5 behavior for `smooth: 0`, even though that is a valid operator-supplied input under the epic and tech design.

Placeholder lower-band behavior is explicit and test-backed: deterministic markers, token accounting, and non-semantic-summary signaling are present and I did not find a hidden model-summary fallback.
productionPathFindings: I did not find a fake writer or fake reload path in the production smart-compact flow itself: the real command path runs async-thread preflight, draft rebuild, PI-target build, atomic write/archive, metadata update, and harness reload, and that path passed `npm run verify-all`.

The production path still includes material compatibility shims: `src/thread/store/file-thread-store.ts:1`, `src/thread/domain/records.ts:1`, `src/thread-view/store/file-thread-view-store.ts:1`, `src/workbench/services/workbench-query-service.ts:1`, and `src/commands/smart-compact.ts:1-4` all still depend on the old `context-*` modules rather than fully relocated Feature 3 surfaces.

blockingFindings.title: Zero-percent smooth allocations still emit smooth-band content
blockingFindings.evidence: `buildDraftThreadView()` writes an explicitly empty smooth selection when the requested smooth budget is 0 (`src/thread-view/services/thread-view-builder.ts:637-646`), but `ThreadViewMaterializer` immediately repopulates any empty smooth band from the full-fidelity boundary via `deriveDefaultSmoothBand()` (`src/thread-view/services/thread-view-materializer.ts:180-217`). A direct repro with `buildDraftThreadView({ requestedLowerBound: 2, requestedBandPercentages: { fullFidelity: 100, smooth: 0, detailed: 0, brief: 0 }, mode: "strict" })` produced `smoothBand.selectedIds = ["turn-oldest","turn-middle-older","turn-middle-newer"]` and emitted three smooth messages, even though the requested smooth allocation was 0%. Because `runSmartCompact()` uses the same builder/materializer path, the generated PI session can contain unrequested smooth-band content.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Story 4 coverage misses the zero-smooth regression
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: The builder test case for the `100/0/0/0` mix (`tests/thread-view/thread-view-builder.test.ts:74-124`) only checks the full-fidelity band and filtered full-fidelity emitted messages. It never asserts that `smoothBand.selectedIds` is empty or that no smooth-band emitted messages exist, so the defect above passes the suite.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Feature 3 surface migration still ships with compatibility shims on the production path
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: The renamed Feature 3 surfaces are partly aliases over older modules instead of fully relocated implementations: `src/thread/store/file-thread-store.ts:1`, `src/thread/domain/records.ts:1`, `src/thread-view/store/file-thread-view-store.ts:1`, and `src/workbench/services/workbench-query-service.ts:1` are re-exports, while `src/thread-view/domain/pi-thread-view-file.ts:1` and `src/commands/smart-compact.ts:1-4` still import from `context-workbench` / `context-steward` directly. This is not a fake execution path, but it is real architecture drift against the tech-design module-boundary cleanup.

unresolvedItems: The fix needs a conscious contract decision: either teach `ThreadViewMaterializer` to distinguish explicit empty smooth selections from legacy defaulting, or stop calling the legacy defaulting path during deterministic rebuilds.

After the builder/materializer contract is corrected, add a command-level regression for `requestedBandPercentages = { fullFidelity: 100, smooth: 0, detailed: 0, brief: 0 }` so the written PI-target file is proven to omit smooth entries as well as the draft view.

crossStoryFindings: Stories compose into the intended deterministic maintenance loop: closed turns get smooth artifacts, chunks close deterministically, closed chunks get explicit placeholder artifacts, rebuilt Thread Views select across all four bands, and smart compact writes and reloads PI-target output.
No cross-story behavioral drift found in the implemented mechanics; the requested gates passed.
architectureFindings: The source/view split is preserved: thread/async-thread owns derived smooth, chunk, and placeholder state; thread-view owns band rebuild and materialization; PI target writing and harness reload remain edge concerns.
Compatibility re-export shims remain for several renamed surfaces, but they point to real implementations rather than fake paths and do not currently block the epic.
epicCoverageAssessment: AC flows 1-6 have direct implementation and test coverage across unit, integration, and E2E suites.
npm run verify passed: 285 unit tests passed with typecheck.
npm run verify-all passed: verify plus 10 integration tests and 34 E2E tests passed.
productionPathFindings: No material fake adapter, placeholder-as-real-summary, or silent no-op production path was found.
Deterministic detailed and brief placeholder outputs are intentional Feature 3 production artifacts and remain explicitly marked as non-semantic placeholders in lower-band and PI-target output.
The PI reload adapter requires a real session-switch dependency and reports PI_RELOAD_FAILED when absent or failed; it does not silently pretend to reload.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Renamed production surfaces still rely on compatibility re-export shims
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Several new surface paths are thin re-exports to context-steward/context-workbench implementations, for example src/thread-view/domain/thread-view-records.ts exports from ../../context-workbench/domain/thread-view-records.js, and src/thread/store/file-thread-store.ts exports from ../../context-steward/store/file-thread-store.js. The tech design allowed temporary compatibility scaffolding, and these are real implementations, not fake adapters.
